section_summary: This section records the narrowing of Japan’s postwar deconcentration program: orders and objections concerning Nippon Soda and Nissan Chemical, followed by State Department analysis of zaibatsu securities sales. It also contains American business criticism of Japanese economic reforms, correspondence about an exclusive cigarette-lighter export arrangement, and SCAP directives governing restricted concerns.

subfiles.title: Final order concerning Nippon Soda reorganization, conclusion
subfiles.from: Holding Company Liquidation Commission
subfiles.about: The order preserves antimonopoly obligations and Commission oversight of Nippon Soda’s reorganization.
subfiles.summary: Concluding provisions retain supervision and jurisdiction over the reorganization.

subfiles.title: Affidavit of publication and service of notice
subfiles.from: Goro Kashima
subfiles.about: Kashima attests to publication and mailing of notice of Nippon Soda’s proposed reorganization order.
subfiles.summary: Records notice published on July 22 and served on interested parties.

subfiles.title: Order cancelling Nippon Soda’s designation
subfiles.from: Holding Company Liquidation Commission
subfiles.about: The Commission cancels Nippon Soda’s designation under the Deconcentration Law.
subfiles.summary: The Commission revokes its earlier order for lack of a readily established prima facie restraint-of-trade case, while preserving creditor rights and Fair Trade Commission authority.

subfiles.title: Objection by non-union Nissan Chemical employees
subfiles.from: Kaichi Yoshida, representative of non-union employees
subfiles.about: Non-union employees oppose the proposed six-company reorganization of Nissan Chemical.
subfiles.summary: They argue that Nissan Chemical has neither restricted competition nor possessed the market power needed to justify deconcentration. The cover page follows the brief’s concluding page in this section.

subfiles.title: Objection by Nissan Chemical labor unions
subfiles.from: Hideo Tsuzi, Satoru Iwaki and Goro Takumi
subfiles.about: Labor union representatives request reconsideration of Nissan Chemical’s proposed breakup.
subfiles.summary: The unions deny excessive concentration, cite workers’ livelihoods and economic recovery, and accept the original order if their plea fails.

subfiles.title: Nissan Chemical company objection
subfiles.from: Sadao Kurobe, Nissan Chemical Industrial Company
subfiles.about: Nissan Chemical contests its designation as an excessive concentration of economic power.
subfiles.summary: Kurobe says the company prepared a six-company plan under earlier criteria but sees no prima facie evidence of restricted competition under the revised principles. He discusses competitors, raw-material constraints, wartime arrangements and acquisitions, and requests transfer of a Reconstruction Financing Bank loan to a successor company.

subfiles.title: Designation of two companies cancelled
subfiles.from: Asahi
subfiles.about: A newspaper reports cancellation of Nippon Soda and Nissan Chemical deconcentration designations.
subfiles.summary: Reports that insufficient evidence of restricted competition led to cancellation, while other economic laws still apply.

subfiles.title: Department file note on Tokyo despatch 741
subfiles.about: The note summarizes the reduced reach of the Deconcentration Law.
subfiles.summary: Notes likely reorganization of only six or seven designated companies and labor opposition.

subfiles.title: State Department routing note
subfiles.about: A handwritten note routes the attached Army correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Routes Draper’s letter and attachment within the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning deconcentration information requested from SCAP
subfiles.from: William H. Draper Jr.
subfiles.about: Draper forwards a message requesting SCAP’s account of deconcentration decisions.
subfiles.summary: Promises State the information when SCAP supplies it and comments on Mr. Herrod’s concerns.

subfiles.title: Message to SCAP requesting deconcentration background
subfiles.from: Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Washington requests the Review Board’s terms of reference and case-by-case grounds for its recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Requests decisions and supporting plans so Washington can explain deconcentration policy to interested parties.

subfiles.title: Department of State charge slip
subfiles.about: A file charge form records circulation of related material.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge slip with little legible substantive content.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting DRF Information Note 238
subfiles.from: Division of Research for Far East
subfiles.about: The memorandum transmits research on zaibatsu securities sales.
subfiles.summary: Warns that conflicting figures prevent a firm answer about securities sales.

subfiles.title: Sale of Zaibatsu Securities in Japan, DRF Information Note 238
subfiles.from: Division of Research for Far East
subfiles.about: The report evaluates conflicting estimates of zaibatsu securities transferred to and sold by liquidation agencies.
subfiles.summary: The report estimates roughly 170 million securities worth ¥7.5 billion subject to liquidation and about 153 million transferred by November 20, 1948. Competing sources put sales at approximately ¥1.04 billion or ¥2.13 billion, implying substantially different completion rates. A table and source notes compare family and holding-company stocks and bonds.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Sale of Zaibatsu Securities in Japan
subfiles.from: Division of Research for Far East
subfiles.about: A second, poorer OCR copy reproduces DRF Information Note 238.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the analysis of securities subject to liquidation, transfers and sales, with its comparative table and footnotes.

subfiles.title: Despatch forwarding restricted-concerns directive
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: A damaged despatch forwards and discusses revised rules for restricted concerns.
subfiles.summary: Describes changes to restricted-concern controls and encloses a SCAP directive.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1983: Regulations Affecting Restricted Concerns
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP consolidates earlier restricted-concern rules and directs retention of amended Imperial Ordinance 657.
subfiles.summary: Rescinds several earlier memoranda without retroactive effect, continues the amended ordinance and directs repeal of a wartime companies law.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch 290 transmitting business-investment report
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards American Chamber of Commerce proposals for revising Japanese economic laws.
subfiles.summary: It summarizes business objections to deconcentration, antimonopoly, labor and zaibatsu-purge measures and compares several proposals with pending Japanese legislation.

subfiles.title: Report of the Sub-Committee on Business Investments
subfiles.from: Jean P. Boyer and Dudley M. Day
subfiles.to: American Chamber of Commerce in Japan
subfiles.about: The report recommends legal changes intended to encourage renewed American business investment in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The authors criticize deconcentration and antimonopoly controls, corporate divestment, labor rules and the zaibatsu personnel purge. They recommend a consolidated antitrust law, greater court oversight, permission for corporate stock investment, narrower statutory labor standards and judicial purge review. They also address patents, taxes, war-loss claims and exchange rates.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch 340 on Chamber approval of the report
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports Chamber approval of the business-investment report after press coverage and criticism.
subfiles.summary: It recounts premature newspaper publicity, Charles Kades’s criticism, and the Chamber’s vote to approve the report by a considerable majority.

subfiles.title: Economic reform laws enforced here criticized
subfiles.from: Rutherford Peats, Nippon Times
subfiles.about: The clipping reports Chamber criticism of Occupation economic reforms.
subfiles.summary: Describes calls to revise antimonopoly, deconcentration, labor and zaibatsu-purge laws and to establish a war-loss claims tribunal.

subfiles.title: Kades charges special interests with trying to scrap SCAP reforms
subfiles.from: United Press
subfiles.about: The clipping reports Kades’s response to Chamber proposals to revise Occupation reforms.
subfiles.summary: Kades defends SCAP reforms, criticizes the Chamber’s report, and links opposition to deconcentration with prewar zaibatsu power.

subfiles.title: Trans Global complaint about cigarette-lighter exports
subfiles.from: J. M. Breen, Trans Global Company
subfiles.about: Trans Global protests an alleged exclusive Japanese export agency that interrupted its cigarette-lighter supply.
subfiles.summary: Breen seeks delivery under an existing contract and equal access to future supplies, citing losses to dealers and distributors.

subfiles.title: Reply to Trans Global Company
subfiles.from: Roger C. Dimon
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the complaint and refers it for investigation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Promises further comment after receiving SCAP’s response.

subfiles.title: Instruction to investigate the Trans Global complaint
subfiles.from: Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: State requests SCAP review of the alleged exclusive lighter-export arrangement.
subfiles.summary: Seeks details on manufacturers, patents, SCAP approval and Trans Global’s outstanding contract.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch 347 forwarding restricted-concern SCAPINs
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards four SCAP memoranda amending controls and releasing restricted companies.
subfiles.summary: Explains the new prior-approval rule and reports releases of 86 and 70 companies from the restricted-concerns schedule.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1983/1: Amendment to Regulations Affecting Restricted Concerns
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP adds a prior-approval requirement for acts under Imperial Ordinance 657.
subfiles.summary: Requires GHQ approval before acts needing the finance minister’s approval.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1991: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP removes a listed group of companies from the restricted-concerns schedule.
subfiles.summary: After citing the directives that added companies to the schedule, the memorandum lists 66 firms for removal across mining, manufacturing, shipping, banking and other industries. The subsequent SCAPIN 1991/1 corrects one entry in this list.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1991/1: Removal of Company from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP corrects the Soyo Rubber entry in SCAPIN 1991.
subfiles.summary: Substitutes Soyo Rubber Industry for the earlier paragraph 2bh entry.
